USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use this week's Washington round with Liu He, Lighthizer, and Mnuchin to test a limited truce—delay or condition the October 15 List 1–3 hike (25% to 30%) and keep December 15 List 4B as leverage rather than firing it blindly. Do not add new tariffs, entity-list designations, or unilateral purchase demands this week; do not roll back existing Lists 1–3 or 4A or loosen Huawei controls without a written, enforceable Chinese offer. Aim for a narrow path (farm/energy purchases plus a pause on scheduled hikes) while keeping structural IP/enforcement text on the table for a later comprehensive deal.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not high. After the May breakdown and August cascade (List 4 announced August 1, Treasury manipulator designation August 5, List 4A at 15% on September 1, China’s ~$75B retaliation including autos), US financial conditions have tightened in a growth-scare way: 10-year yields fell from 2.55% (April 15) to 1.59% (October 9), fed funds were cut from 2.39% to 1.83%, Michigan sentiment crashed from 100 in May to 89.8 in August before only a partial rebound to 95.5, VIX is 18.64 vs ~12 in mid-April, and industrial production is slightly weaker. US goods exports to China remain depressed (~$8.9B in October vs ~$39.8B of imports), so farm-belt and other export constituencies are still absorbing China’s retaliation even after Beijing’s mid-September soybean/pork exemption signal and 16-item exemption list. That is a material political and sectoral hit, not an existential supply-chain or recession event—CPI is only modestly higher, the goods trade deficit has actually narrowed, and China’s IP is still expanding (~4.7% y/y) with stable reserves, so Beijing is not collapsing into a concession. The opportunity side of the ledger is also real: the US already delayed the October 1 hike to October 15 as goodwill, List 4B (phones, laptops, toys) is still unused leverage into the holiday season, and Huawei remains on the Entity List. Escalating into a live negotiating week would likely recreate the post-Shanghai August spiral and invite further farm/auto retaliation plus a consumer-price hit if List 4B is pulled forward. Full or partial rollback now would throw away leverage after China walked back structural text in May and is publicly talking down this round (“talk while fighting,” shortened stay, no “special envoy” title). Negotiate without new commitments is therefore the stance that matches a moderate, two-sided threat.
key_factors: 13th-round Washington talks (Liu He / Lighthizer / Mnuchin) are underway or imminent with low official expectations and a live Oct 15 25%→30% hike deadline
Existing US tariffs already cover Lists 1–3 at 25% plus List 4A at 15%; List 4B (consumer electronics/apparel) remains unused leverage until Dec 15
US financial/growth scare: 10Y 1.59%, Fed easing, August sentiment crash, elevated VIX — trade war is biting expectations more than hard output so far
US exports to China remain weak; China’s farm/auto retaliation is the main US political vulnerability, only partially eased by Sept exemptions and reported new farm orders
Structural issues (IP, forced tech transfer, enforcement, subsidies) remain unresolved after the May collapse; China is not offering a comprehensive package
Huawei Entity List and rare-earth signaling keep a non-tariff escalation channel open on both sides; using it now would poison talks

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump tweets negotiations going too slowly; orders List 3 to 25% on May 10 and preparation of tariffs on remaining ~$300B.
US Commerce adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List; US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
USTR splits List 4: 4A effective Sept 1; 4B (cell phones, laptops, toys, apparel) delayed to Dec 15; some sensitive items excluded.
China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods including re-imposing tariffs on US autos; Trump orders firms to look for alternatives to China and a 5-point List 4 hike.
List 4A takes effect at 15%; China’s first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
China announces first tariff-exemption list for some US products (16 categories; industrial inputs/chemicals — not a broad farm rollback).
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
US 10-year yield latest 1.59% on 2019-10-09, down ~96 bp / -37.6% over the lookback — growth-scare pricing.
Federal funds effective rate cut from 2.39% (May) to 1.83% (October).
Michigan consumer sentiment fell from 100 (May) to 89.8 (August), recovered only to 95.5 (October).
US goods exports to China latest ~$8.85B (Oct) vs imports from China ~$39.8B — export channel still compressed.
VIX 18.64 on 2019-10-09 vs ~12.3 in mid-April; spiked to 24.59 on August 5 during the FX/tariff shock.
Trump delayed the hike on ~$250B of Chinese goods from Oct 1 to Oct 15 (25% to 30%) as a goodwill gesture at Liu He’s request around China’s 70th anniversary.

Oct 8: China tones down expectations for this week’s 13th round; Liu He not titled special envoy; possible shortened stay; “talk while fighting”; Trump still prefers a comprehensive deal over a mini-deal.
Talks restarted after the Lighthizer/Mnuchin–Liu He call; sides still split on cybertheft, tech transfer, SOE subsidies, and enforceable structural text after the May collapse.
